clusters.text: Streets in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo filled with crowds dressed in green, yellow, and red, celebrating democracy and unity. Fireworks lit up the night sky in Brazilian cities as supporters of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva poured into the streets to celebrate his dramatic re-election victory on Sunday. In Rio de Janeiro, vuvuzelas echoed along the beachfront and central avenues as crowds draped in Brazil’s green-and-yellow flag and Lula’s trademark red danced, sang campaign songs and chanted pro-democracy slogans. In Sao Paulo, thousands of people dressed in red, the colour of Lula’s Workers’ Party, packed central squares and major roads, waving banners and setting off flares in scenes reminiscent of football title celebrations. According to official results, Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, secured an unprecedented fourth term with 51.8 percent of the vote against 48.2 percent for his far-right rival, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Lula hailed the high turnout, saying Brazilians had “voted to defend democracy”. The jubilation unfolded despite Bolsonaro’s refusal to accept the result, promising to seek to annul the vote after a Supreme Court decision extended polling by two hours. But in city after city, Lula’s supporters treated the win as a resounding repudiation of authoritarianism and a renewed mandate for Brazil’s left.

clusters.text: Watch: Why Israel's election is one of the most important in its history After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming. The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight. Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote. On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government. "We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out." This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face. Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders? Israel's far right find fertile ground among first-time voters The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician". But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law. Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country. I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors. One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before. The rupee weakened through the morning, slipping 0.18 per cent to 95.1150 per dollar by 11:10 a.m. IST. Brent crude rose more than 6 per cent last week to a six-month high amid concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on Saudi Arabia. Prices remained near $115 a barrel in Asia trading. High oil prices widen India’s import bill, add to inflationary pressures and weigh on economic growth. They can encourage companies to increase currency hedges and make foreign investors more cautious about Indian assets. The rupee had found support in recent weeks from the Reserve Bank of India’s interventions, which helped it recover from levels near 96.70 per dollar, and from Jio Platforms IPO-linked inflows. In the absence of this support, the currency remains more exposed to dollar demand. Another factor could come into play this week, with the Federal Reserve’s policy decision adding to the rupee’s list of external risks. A rate pause is widely expected, leaving markets focused on guidance on the rate outlook and whether further tightening remains on the table this year. India’s foreign exchange reserves fell for a sixth consecutive week through October 16, declining by $5 billion to $721 billion. clusters.text: Eric Bauza, the voice artist behind Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died aged 46. A statement from the Emmy award-winning star's family posted on Instagram , external said he had died "suddenly". Bauza had voiced a number of characters in this summer's animated hit Coyote vs. Acme, and appeared in the recent release Forgotten Island. Variety reports that the cause of death was hypertensive cardiovascular disease and that Bauza died at home on Sunday. In a 2021 interview with NBC News, Bauza, who was born in Ontario and was of Filipino descent, said he grew up a huge fan of the Looney Tunes characters and used to copy the voices as a child. "Looney Tunes transcends all languages and all cultures," he said , external . "It doesn't matter what part of the planet you're from. You get the comedy." He voiced Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Elmer Fudd and Foghorn Leghorn in 2021's Space Jam: A New Legacy before reprising those roles and that of Road Runner in Coyote vs. Acme. He also played the part of Toad General in 2023's The Super Mario Bros. Movie and its sequel The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, the fifth highest-grossing film internationally this year. Between 2022 and 2025, he won three Emmy awards for outstanding voice performance in a number of TV series. In a statement reported by the Hollywood Reporter , external , Channing Dungey, the chairman of Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks, said: "Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. "He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. clusters.text: Researchers found a malicious AGENTS markdown instruction file in a customer’s Downloads folder that tricked an AI coding agent into installing a rogue npm package. They reproduced the attack against OpenAI Codex and demonstrated a related technique against Claude Code to leak OAuth tokens and hijack the account using only the malicious instructions. Markdown files such as AGENTS.md are plain-text files that contain project-specific instructions for AI coding agents, such as the tools to use, how to run tests, and the coding conventions to follow. Researchers at Forever Security, a company that monitors for risks introduced by AI agents and autonomous software, discovered the tactic on a customer’s computer, where a coding agent attempted to install the malicious npm package ‘ function-color .’ The investigation traced the AI agent’s attempt to install a malicious npm package to an AGENTS.md file in the customer’s ~/Downloads folder, which also served as the agent’s working directory. Agents automatically load applicable files from their working directory and use the contained instructions to guide their actions. While these files aren’t executables, malicious instructions contained in them can lead to AI agents running commands, installing packages, or changing settings using the tools and permissions available to it. "There is nothing here for OpenAI or Anthropic to patch. An agent that follows the AGENTS.md in its folder is doing exactly what it was built to do," the researchers say . The researchers' test confirmed that an attacker could use such a file to manipulate OpenAI Codex and Claude Code into executing code or stealing credentials. Although the researchers could not determine how the malicious instructions file landed into the target's ~/Downloads location, they explained to BleepingComputer that simply visiting a malicious page could drop a payload without any user interaction. In a report this week, Forever Security says that "~/Downloads is special. clusters.text: Prayagraj: To ensure safe and hassle-free train travel, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) in Prayagraj division has arrested over 1,200 people this year for unauthorised entry onto railway tracks and illegal e-ticketing.Between Jan 1 and Oct 15, the RPF arrested 1,188 people for trespassing on railway tracks and initiated action against them. The drive is aimed at preventing accidents caused by people crossing or entering railway tracks.The highest number of arrests was recorded in March, when 259 people were held, followed by May (226) and April (164). The RPF arrested 131 people in Jan, 109 in Feb, 98 in June, 40 in July, 43 in Aug, 111 in Sept and seven till Oct 15, said Prayagraj division PRO Amit Kumar Singh.Among RPF posts, Prayagraj Junction recorded the highest number of arrests at 141, followed by Chunar (120), Kanpur Central (119), Naini (99), Fatehpur (95) and Prayagraj Chheoki (88). Kanpur Anwarganj accounted for 65 arrests, while Panki Dham, Phaphund and Aligarh recorded 55 each.In a separate drive under Operation Uplabdh, the RPF registered 12 cases of illegal e-ticketing between Jan and Sept and arrested 17 people. It recovered 69 e-tickets worth ₹2.54 lakh and got 18 personal user IDs and one agent ID blocked for alleged misuse.In Sept alone, three cases were registered, three people were arrested and 23 tickets worth ₹39,399 were recovered. Three personal IDs were also blocked.Officials said the drive aims to protect genuine passengers’ access to reservations while preventing unauthorised ticket sales and the misuse of personal IDs.Railway authorities have appealed to passengers and the public not to cross tracks under any circumstances and to use foot overbridges, subways or other designated routes. Passengers have also been advised to book tickets only through authorised channels and report illegal e-ticketing activities to the RPF.

clusters.title: “A lot of emotion, unexpected…” – Musetti ends seven-final losing streak and four-year title drought by beating Fritz in Lyon
clusters.snippet: Lorenzo Musetti won the title on Sunday afternoon against Taylor Fritz.
also: Musetti downs Fritz in Lyon for ‘dream’ first title in four years
clusters.text: Lorenzo Musetti won the title on Sunday afternoon against Taylor Fritz. For more than two years, a final had been the one match Lorenzo Musetti could not win. He had lost seven in a row on the ATP Tour since his last title in 2022. On Sunday in Lyon, a day after saving four match points against Flavio Cobolli, the Italian finally put an end to that run, beating second seed Taylor Fritz 6-3, 6-4 to win the Lyon ATP 250. “Totally unexpected. For me, it’s such a roller coaster,” Musetti said on court. “The previous matches have been incredible. I saved four match points to play a fantastic final. I have to say that honestly, before stepping on the court, I was feeling pain everywhere. But then when I stepped on court, I started to think and focus on the match. I think I played probably my best tennis, so I’m really happy and proud of this win.” He credited his resilience, and the people who kept him going through a draining week. “The spirit of fighting, I guess, was the key for this tournament, because I always had an incredible attitude,” he said. “I have to say thanks to my team, to the medical staff and the physio, who tried to get me back in shape even after hours and hours of matches. Today I probably felt more relaxed inside my head, and my tennis went more fluid. It was a really great performance.” “It’s a mess. It’s a lot of emotion. I don’t know how to describe it, but I feel that it’s such a dream that I don’t want to wake up,” Musetti added. “I’m still dreaming, so I’m really happy, and now I will have some days to enjoy the win.” The No. 6 seed did it with authority. Fritz had not lost his serve all week, and Musetti broke him in his first service game. He took a 3-0 lead and closed out the set on his first set point. In the second set he broke again at 2-1, on his third break point, then held through a long game for 3-1 and served out the match on his first match point. He did not face a break point. It is the third title of Musetti’s career, after Hamburg and Naples in 2022, and the first by an Italian in the history of the tournament, which was held in Marseille from 1993 to 2025. He becomes the fourth Italian to win an ATP Tour title this season, after Jannik Sinner, Cobolli and Luciano Darderi. The week came after a difficult season. clusters.title: Jharkhand: Revenue sub-inspector ‘murdered’ at his house in Ranchi, probe underway
also: Ranchi Revenue Officer Murdered at Home, Investigation Underway
clusters.text:
Ranchi, Oct 25 (PTI) A 40-year-old revenue department official was allegedly killed at his house in Jharkhand’s Ranchi by unidentified persons, police said on Sunday.

The incident occurred in Tetar Tola within Namkum police station limits on Saturday.

The deceased was identified as Lakshmikant Munda, a resident of Bundu Block, who was posted at the Argora Circle Office as a revenue sub-inspector, they said.

"Munda was attacked and killed by unidentified persons at his house. The incident came to light when he did not reach office, and was not responding to phone calls. Post-mortem examination of the victim will be conducted on Sunday," Namkum police station officer-in-charge Ramnarayan told PTI.

Police have launched a detailed investigation into the murder, and are investigating the case from all angles, including robbery and old enmity, he said.

Injury marks were found on the victim's head, while the DVR containing the CCTV footage of the house was missing, the officer added.

“An SIT is probing the matter, and the culprits will soon be nabbed,” Ranchi Rural SP Gaurav Goswami told PTI.

Meanwhile, former chief minister and BJP leader Arjun Munda met the victim's family members at RIMS and expressed condolences.

He demanded an impartial probe into the case and strict action against the culprits.

“If a government official is not safe in his house in the state capital, who will assure security to the common citizens of the state?” Munda said. PTI RPS RG RPS RBT

clusters.title: Ranchi: Woman with four children threatens self-immolation at SSP’s residence, detained
clusters.text: Ranchi, Oct 25 (IANS) Chaos and commotion erupted outside the Senior Superintendent of Police’s (SSP) residence in the Jharkhand capital on Sunday as a woman with her four children threatened self-immolation in protest against police ‘inaction’ over the disappearance of one of her children. The woman alleged that one of her children went missing from Ranchi Sadar Hospital and, despite repeated requests, the police personnel were not assisting her. The woman, who was in utter distress and despair amid her persistent efforts to find the child and repeated appeals to the police and administration, said that she had decided to take this extreme step. The police personnel stationed at the site immediately took the woman into custody, while her children were also placed under police protection. The woman is a resident of the Hehal-Bajra area in Ranchi. She arrived at the SSP’s residence in Morabadi with her four children on Sunday, seeking to voice her anger and frustration over the lack of action regarding her missing child. It was during this time that she attempted self-immolation. Upon learning of the incident, security personnel and officials present at the scene intervened immediately. According to the woman, her child went missing from Sadar Hospital about a year ago, and she has been searching for the child ever since. She had sought assistance from the police and the administration, but no information regarding the child has surfaced to date. The woman stated that she is deeply distressed and frustrated due to the prolonged disappearance of her child. Following her detention, the Station House Officer (SHO) of the Lalpur police station is gathering details regarding her allegations and the circumstances surrounding the child’s disappearance. However, any official intimation is yet to come regarding the circumstances under which the child went missing or the actions taken so far to locate the child. The subsequent steps taken by the police and the investigation by the relevant authorities are now considered crucial in the search for the missing child.

But when the Prayagraj resident bought a Maruti Alto in 2011, he found that owning a conventional car did not solve his problem. His disability, which affects his legs, prevented him from driving it.Instead of giving up on the idea of travelling independently, Kishore decided to build a vehicle suited to his needs. clusters.text: A case has come to light in Prayagraj in which a woman professor has accused a university registrar and legal adviser of verbal abuse and death threats. The allegations have been levelled against Registrar SS Mishra and Legal Adviser Sarvesh Mishra. Assistant Professor Dr Vandana Mishra said, “I was misbehaved with on 11 September. The legal adviser tried to hit me after taking off his shoe. I was threatened with dismissal from my job and the destruction of my career.” An FIR was registered on Sunday, 44 days after the alleged incident. The case falls under the jurisdiction of Sarai Inayat police station. Dr Vandana Mishra has been working as an assistant professor at Nehru Gram Bharati Deemed University since 2019 and also heads the Department of Special Education. She said that on 11 September, between approximately 2.30pm and 5pm, she visited the office of Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof. Suresh Chandra Tiwari for departmental work related to admissions to the D.Ed Special Education (HI) course. The university’s legal adviser, Sarvesh Mishra, was also present. According to Dr Vandana, Sarvesh Mishra called Acting Registrar SS Mishra and asked him to come to the office after seeing her. She told the Pro Vice-Chancellor that the application and the necessary formalities had not been completed on time in 2025. As a result, the approval process for the D.Ed Special (HI) and M.Ed Special (HI) courses could not be completed. She said that if the relevant file and documents were made available, the application process for the next academic session could be completed. In her complaint, Dr Vandana Mishra alleged that Executive Registrar SS Mishra behaved inappropriately towards her, verbally abused her and threatened to kill her.
